title: Implement PWA enhancements: offline mode, splash screen, caching, install UX, and standalone polish

requirements.text: Add offline support for the PWA by implementing a service worker that precaches the app shell and provides a clear offline fallback behavior when the network is unavailable.

quotes: Can we implement all of these except for app shortcuts

acceptanceCriteria: A service worker is registered by the app and becomes active after first load (with standard update/refresh behavior).
Key static assets required to render the UI shell are precached so that reopening the installed app without network still loads the shell.
When the user is offline, the app shows a clear offline state (e.g., dedicated offline screen or persistent banner) rather than failing silently.
Offline behavior does not require backend changes and does not break authenticated flows when online.

requirements.text: Improve caching/performance via a smarter service-worker caching strategy (e.g., precache for core assets and appropriate runtime caching rules) to reduce load time and improve repeat visits.

quotes: Can we implement all of these except for app shortcuts

acceptanceCriteria: Core UI assets (HTML/app bundle/CSS and other stable assets) are served quickly on repeat visits via cache.
Runtime caching rules avoid serving stale HTML indefinitely (ensure users still receive new deployments).
Caching strategy does not interfere with Internet Identity authentication flow or canister calls (no caching of authenticated API responses unless explicitly safe).

requirements.text: Create and integrate a custom PWA splash screen that matches the app branding, including iOS startup images and required metadata/link tags.

quotes: Can we implement all of these except for app shortcuts

acceptanceCriteria: `frontend/index.html` includes the appropriate iOS splash/startup image `<link rel="apple-touch-startup-image" ...>` entries referencing generated static assets.
Splash screen assets are stored in `frontend/public/assets/generated` and referenced directly from the frontend (not served through the backend).
When launched from the home screen on iOS, the splash screen displays instead of a blank white/black screen (device support limited to the included sizes).

requirements.text: Implement a better install prompt UX: provide a more noticeable, helpful install entry point and guidance for platforms where the native `beforeinstallprompt` is unavailable (e.g., iOS).

quotes: Can we implement all of these except for app shortcuts

acceptanceCriteria: Users who are not installed can discover an install call-to-action without needing to find it incidentally.
When `beforeinstallprompt` is available, the UX triggers the native prompt via the existing hook behavior.
When `beforeinstallprompt` is not available (common on iOS), the UX shows clear English instructions for installing via the browser share/menu flow.
The install UX does not appear when the app is already running in standalone mode.

requirements.text: Polish the standalone (installed) layout so the PWA feels native: handle safe-area insets, prevent awkward scrolling/overflow, and ensure header/navigation spacing looks correct in standalone mode on mobile.

quotes: Can we implement all of these except for app shortcuts

acceptanceCriteria: In standalone mode on mobile, key layout regions (TopBar/Navigation/Main) respect safe-area insets and do not overlap notches/home indicators.
The app avoids unintended double scrollbars and preserves expected full-height layout behavior.
Changes do not require editing files listed as immutable in SYSTEM_CONTEXT.

constraints: Do not implement PWA app shortcuts.
Do not change the PWA manifest icon `src` values away from the provided external image URL in `frontend/public/manifest.webmanifest`.
Do not edit files under `frontend/src/components/ui` or any paths listed in `frontend.immutablePaths` from SYSTEM_CONTEXT.
Use English for all user-facing text.
nonGoals: Backend (Motoko) feature work or schema changes for these PWA enhancements.
Third-party authentication providers (only Internet Identity is supported).
